title: Starting again is a skill
description: Anyone can start once; the people who succeed long-term are the ones who get good at starting again after a gap.

body.heading: The gap is not the end of the story
paragraphs: Almost every worthwhile habit or goal includes gaps: the fortnight of illness, the chaotic month, the holiday that scattered every routine. We tend to treat the gap as the moment the story ended. In reality, the gap is just a chapter most stories have.
What separates people who keep going from people who do not is rarely the length of their gaps. It is the speed and kindness of their restarts.

body.heading: Make the restart embarrassingly small
paragraphs: The first session back should be so easy it feels almost silly: one page, five minutes, the shortest route. The purpose is not fitness or progress; it is proof. You are showing yourself that the door still opens.
Resist the urge to “make up for” the gap with a heroic effort. Heroic restarts usually cause soreness, dread and a second gap. A gentle restart causes a second day, and a third.

body.heading: Remove the apology from restarting
paragraphs: You do not need to explain the gap to anyone, including yourself. No confession, no fresh diary bought as penance, no waiting for Monday or the first of the month. An ordinary Tuesday afternoon is a perfectly good place to begin again.
Each restart makes the next one easier, because you build a personal history of returning. Eventually the gaps stop frightening you. You know how this goes: life interrupts, and then you start again.

takeaway: Practise the restart until it is boring: small, kind, and without apology.
